- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to match true decline.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average of prior 5 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2 day lag correction: forecast = true value from 2 days prior + 0.5×(true - prior) for next day.  
- For long-term (30-day) forecasts, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 7–10 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 7 days.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
